scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-01.statement: Field route completion for manual meter reads was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug-Sep 2026, affecting 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Dispute ticket response times across 2440 tickets are within SLA: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-03.statement: Monthly dispute ticket volume was stable (~590-610) in Jun-Jul 2026 then roughly doubled to 1180 in Aug and 1260 in Sep 2026.

F-04.statement: Of disputed bills, 1240 are from ESTIMATED reads and 1785 are from ACTUAL reads (3025 total).

F-05.statement: Billing-db tariff_change_log contains zero records for this year, confirming authoritatively that no tariff change occurred.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, but such changes are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log lagging_routes query found 14 lagging routes with distinct completion values, including a sample completion of 0.70 for route R-00.

F-08.statement: 320 accounts received an estimated bill in the last billing cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes.

F-09.statement: Of 1240 AMI-channel read events behind ESTIMATED disputed bills, 1184 had an AMI read before cutoff exported to billing but rejected with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 had no AMI read received (NO_READ_RECEIVED, not exported).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-AI-AUTOFIX-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is a billing-defect problem that an AI agent can both diagnose and remediate by auto-answering tickets and fixing the underlying bill-generation fault.

H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT.statement: A billing import validation rule changed around August is incorrectly rejecting valid reads or forcing estimate substitution, producing systematically wrong bills.

H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: The AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) started failing or delivering invalid reads around August, causing more estimated/wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL.statement: Contracted manual meter reading (ORG-FIELD) has had declining route completion since August, increasing estimate substitution and wrong bills, as SH-FIELD's staffing framing suggests.

H-NONBILLING-CS-RESPONSE.statement: Bills are not actually more wrong than before; the ticket count doubled because of a CRM/CS-side change (e.g., slower response or process change) that increases filing/reopening, independent of billing accuracy.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECTION-R.statement: The billing import validation step specifically rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution for those accounts and accounting for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route completion for manual reads in Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — a measurable shortfall in completed manual read routes during the dispute-surge period, but no trend data or linkage to disputes/estimates is shown yet.

CS ticket response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, so the dispute surge is not being driven by CS responding more slowly; this observation says nothing about whether bills themselves are correct or about the ticket-volume doubling itself.

CRM data shows dispute tickets were stable near 590-610/month in Jun-Jul 2026 and roughly doubled to 1180 in Aug and 1260 in Sep 2026, confirming an abrupt onset in August that persisted (and slightly grew) into September; this quantifies CL-01's 'doubled since August' claim but does not by itself attribute the cause to billing errors, field reads, AMI delivery, a rule change, or CS process.

Disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL reads, so the majority (59%) of disputed bills belong to customers whose bills were based on an actual meter read, not an estimate. This weakens estimate-substitution pathways (field-read shortfall, AMI delivery failure) as the dominant explanation for the dispute surge and points toward a billing-side defect that also affects actual-read bills.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (an interested party per the staffing-attribution bias noted in stakeholders) claims a shortfall of three readers since July causes late routes, which in turn causes estimated bills for those customers. This is an unverified stakeholder claim offering a mechanism for route lateness, but it does not address why E-04 shows the majority (59%) of disputed bills come from ACTUAL, not estimated, reads.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims there has been no tariff change this year, an unverified stakeholder statement (authority NON_AUTHORITATIVE) that, if true, would rule out a rate/tariff change as a cause of wrong bills during the dispute surge; it says nothing about import validation rules, read types, AMI delivery, or field staffing.

An authoritative, complete query of billing-db's tariff_change_log found zero records for this year, independently confirming no tariff change occurred and corroborating SH-BILL's claim (CL-03) and prior stakeholder-sourced evidence (E-06) with a system-of-record check.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms the utility may request route priority changes but execution requires prior confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, corroborating the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update. It is an authorization/governance document and does not speak to the billing-defect causal chain under investigation.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log lagging_routes query returns 14 individual routes with distinct completion values (sample completion 0.70 for route R-00), giving route-level granularity beneath the aggregate 0.88 completion rate (E-01). It shows which specific routes are lagging but does not link any route to the composition (ACTUAL vs ESTIMATED) of disputed bills.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-db's accounts_estimated_last_cycle query (E-10) returns 320 distinct accounts across 40 distinct routes that received an estimated bill in the last cycle; the record only carries account_id and route, with no reason/import-status/tariff field, so it supports the templates work item (W-WI-TEMPLATES) but cannot by itself link these estimated accounts to lagging routes (E-09) or to the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills (E-04).

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (a stakeholder, not an authoritative system check) reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned today per vendor ticket TX-4471. This is an unverified claim that the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query may now be runnable; it does not itself supply any AMI read data or confirm data quality/completeness.

Of 1240 AMI-channel read events behind the ESTIMATED-type disputed bills, 1184 had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but were REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at billing import, while only 56 had no AMI read received at all. All records are read_channel=AMI, so the estimate-substitution behind most ESTIMATED disputes traces to billing import rejecting valid high-consumption reads, not AMI delivery failure or manual field-read shortfall.

proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix wrong bills after tickets roughly doubled since August (CL-01). Investigation established the real problem (PD-1): tickets jumped from a stable ~600/month baseline (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-03), and the best-supported mechanism is a billing-import validation rule change around August rejecting valid reads (H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT, SUPPORTED). This was established by ruling out alternatives: CS response times stayed within SLA (E-02); no tariff change occurred (E-07, corroborating E-06/CL-03); and 59% of disputed bills come from ACTUAL (not estimated) reads (E-04), contradicting pure field-staffing-shortfall or AMI-delivery-failure explanations (both REJECTED against E-04/E-12). A deeper check (E-12) found 1184 of 1240 AMI reads behind ESTIMATED disputes were valid reads received before cutoff but REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at billing import, directly supporting the rule-change-defect theory. The release delivered read-only diagnostic and support capability only: the ACTUAL/ESTIMATED dispute-bill breakdown (E-04), dispute-volume trend monitoring (E-03), route-completion trend monitoring (E-01), and dispute-response templates for CS — with no automated bill writes, since that requires Billing Operations authority (K-BILLWRITE). The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the DEFINE gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS because the single most decisive remaining check — querying the billing-config rule-change log to confirm the August change — could not be executed; it is tracked as an open, blocking verification obligation (VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION) outside this release's scope. Everything released rests on the as-yet-unconfirmed H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT hypothesis, not a confirmed root cause.
